intro: An AI assistant for music producers is a voice helper that sees your screen and answers while you work. Lazur is one for the Mac. Hold ⌥⌘, ask your question, and Lazur answers out loud. It points at controls, guides you one click at a time and drafts text when you need words. It does not click for you.
tldr: Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask about anything on screen.
It points at settings in Logic Pro, Ableton Live, Pro Tools and your browser. It guides you one click at a time.
It does not click buttons, edit files or act as a plugin for any DAW.
Check version requirements before you update. Pro Tools 2026.11 and Logic Pro 13.0 both shipped in early November 2026.
Audio and screenshots go to AI providers to answer and are not stored. Check your client agreement first.

blocks.text: Most producers do not work a standard office day. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics says 48% of musicians and singers are self-employed. It also says their schedules are often irregular. Many find only part-time or intermittent work. That mix sets the pattern for everything below.
Where a producer's day goes

No study found measures how producers split a working day between the DAW, email, admin and marketing. This page will not give you a precise percentage, because none exists. It will show you the parts of the day the sources do support.

Start with self-employment. Nearly half of the people in this trade run their own business. That means client email, licensing questions and invoices sit next to the music. Nobody handles them for you unless you hire help.

Interruptions are the other part. Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index covered 31,000 full-time knowledge workers in 31 markets. The average worker got 117 emails a day. Employees were interrupted 275 times a day during core hours. Producers are not office workers, so read these figures as context, not as your own numbers.

EDMProd asked producers what they struggle with most. The article reports 1,097 answers to that question. Marketing and promotion appear in the list. The list is not ranked, and no time share is given. So you can say marketing is a struggle, but not how many hours it takes. Treat that as a reason to measure your own week for two weeks.
The admin that lands in the middle of a session

The pattern usually runs like this. You open the session at 10:00 and finally get into a groove. A client asks for a bounce. A sync house wants the licensing terms. You answer the email, then come back to a session that has lost its place.

Here is a worked example. A label asks whether a beat you sold last year can go into a TV pitch. Your reply is due at 17:00. The license is a PDF open in Chrome. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask: 'What does this license say about sync use?' Lazur reads the screen and answers out loud. Then hold fn and dictate your reply at the cursor.

Treat the answer as a reading aid. Find the clause yourself before you promise anything. A wrong promise to a label costs far more than the ten minutes you saved. Keep the PDF open so you can check each phrase Lazur mentions.
Which DAW version to check before you update

Versions move fast. Pro Tools 2026.11 came out on November 3, 2026. Logic Pro 13.0 followed on November 5, 2026. Ableton Live 12.4.16 landed on October 30, 2026. Check the requirements before you click update, not after your session refuses to open.

blocks.text: Ableton's notes show that 12.4.16 lists a Windows install fix only. The macOS fixes sit in 12.4.15, dated October 28, 2026. Those cover a shutdown crash when you press ⌘Q with a plug-in window focused, a crash when an audio device disconnects, and wrong latency values after a sample rate change. I could not confirm the minimum macOS version for Live 12, because Ableton's system requirements page did not load.

Logic Pro 13 has a built-in Intelligent Assistant. It is not part of the one-time price. Production Expert reports it needs an Apple Creator Studio subscription, an Apple silicon Mac and macOS 27 or later. It is marked beta and works in English only. Logic 13 costs $199.99 one-time in the US, or comes with Creator Studio at $12.99 a month or $129 a year. Existing owners get the update free.

Pro Tools 2026.11 needs at least 16GB of RAM and 15GB of free space for installation. It needs one or more dedicated audio drives. Avid lists an M1 or newer Apple silicon chip, or an Intel Dual Core i5 or faster. Earlier macOS versions are untested, so stay on a listed version.

blocks.title: Check your Mac first
blocks.text: Open Apple menu > About This Mac before you install a DAW update. Then read the requirements list for that exact version, not the one from last year.
Voice help in Chrome and Slack

A lot of producing happens in a browser. Sample stores, label portals, distributor dashboards and forums all live there. Hold ⌥⌘ on any page and ask about it. Lazur explains what is on screen, points at the part you need and answers out loud. You keep the clicks.

Slack is where collaborators send mix notes. Ask Lazur to explain a note from your vocalist in plain words. Then hold fn and dictate the reply. Dictation types clean text at your cursor in any app, so you can answer in the thread without typing every word.

If Chrome takes most of your attention, read [Chrome for music producers](/for/music-producers/chrome). For channel-based feedback and mix notes, read [Slack for music producers](/for/music-producers/slack).
How to use Lazur in your DAW, step by step

items: Open the DAW window you need, such as the mixer, the browser or the arrangement view.
Hold ⌥⌘ and ask a question that names the thing. Try: Where is Bounce in this Logic window?
Watch for the circle and label. Lazur draws them on your screen when it points.
For a longer job, say: Walk me through it. Lazur guides one click at a time and waits for each click.
Hold fn when you need text in a note, email or chat. Dictation types it at the cursor.

blocks.text: Here is a guided example. Say you want a ceiling on a limiter on your master bus. Hold ⌥⌘ and say: Walk me through setting the ceiling on this limiter. Lazur points at the first control and waits. You click it. Then it points at the next one. You stay in control of the session the whole time.

blocks.title: Lazur does not click for you
blocks.text: Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps. Plan each session as if you still do the clicks, because you do.
Mistakes producers make with AI help

items: Asking a vague question. Help me finish this track gives a vague answer. Ask Where is the bounce option? instead.
Guessing which build fixes your problem. Read the release notes before you update. Ableton's 12.4.16 notes list a Windows-only change, so a Mac user can skip it, while 12.4.15 holds the macOS fixes.
Expecting Lazur to change your session. It points and guides. It does not edit files or click for you.
Sending unreleased client audio without a check. Read your agreement first. Audio goes to AI providers to answer and is not stored.
Skipping the trial. Test on a real session during the 3-day Pro trial, not on a demo file.

blocks.text: Privacy and client work

Client material needs care. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. Those files are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

That does not replace your contract. Your client agreement decides what you can share and with whom. Read it before you open unreleased stems while Lazur is listening, especially if a collaborator's files are in the same window.
Keep the screen clean. Lazur sees what is on screen. If a private file or a chat with a client is open, close it or move it out of view before you hold the shortcut.
What a realistic day looks like with Lazur

The day below shows seven moments. Each one is a short question, not a long chat. Most of them replace a search, a PDF scroll or a note you would otherwise write to yourself. Notice that you ask in plain words. You do not need the menu names first.
What to do next

Start with one job. Pick the question you ask most often, such as where a setting is or what a license says. Test it on a real session for a day. If it saves you time, keep going. If it does not, try a different question.
Download Lazur for macOS from the [download page](/download). Check plan details on the [pricing page](/pricing). The 3-day Pro trial starts when you first open the app, and it needs no credit card.

faq.question: Is Lazur a plugin for Logic Pro or Ableton Live?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app. It runs on your Mac, lives in the notch and answers when you hold ⌥⌘. It does not edit your session or click buttons for you.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my project or bounce my mix?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at the control, explains it, or guides you one click at a time. You do the clicking. It does not edit files or operate other apps for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. If your studio runs a Windows machine, Lazur does not cover it yet.

faq.question: Does Lazur listen to my studio all the time?
faq.answer: No. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: How is Lazur different from Logic Pro's Intelligent Assistant?
faq.answer: Logic Pro 13 has its own Intelligent Assistant. Production Expert reports it needs Creator Studio, Apple silicon and macOS 27 or later, and it is in beta and English only. Lazur works in any app on your Mac, so it also covers Chrome, Slack and Gmail.

faq.question: Is there a free way to try it?
faq.answer: Lazur has a 3-day Pro trial. It starts when you first open the app, and no credit card is needed. Check the pricing page for plan details after the trial.

painPoints.title: Admin that lands mid-session
painPoints.text: Client emails, licensing questions and invoices arrive while the session is open. Self-employed producers answer them alone, with no assistant to hand them to.

painPoints.title: Interruptions from every app
painPoints.text: Microsoft's 2025 survey found 117 emails a day and 275 interruptions during core hours for knowledge workers. The study did not cover producers, but Slack, Gmail and the browser pull at you the same way.

painPoints.title: Marketing nobody trained you for
painPoints.text: EDMProd's survey lists marketing and promotion among the biggest struggles. It drew 1,097 answers to that question, and it does not rank the struggles or give time shares.

painPoints.title: Version churn before a deadline
painPoints.text: Pro Tools 2026.11 arrived on November 3, 2026, and Logic Pro 13.0 on November 5. Each update can change menus and requirements, so checking takes time you did not plan for.

painPoints.title: Irregular work and thin margins
painPoints.text: The BLS says musicians often have irregular schedules, and many find only part-time or intermittent work. Less steady work means more admin falls on you.
